ideas.title: Non-coder Claude Skills + Claude Code marketing systems desk
ideas.one_liner: Productize Skills as portable instruction manuals so non-technical operators ship marketing systems in Claude Code/Cursor without learning to code.
ideas.evidence_quote: I come from a non-technical background. Years ago I tried to learn to code — very unsuccessfully. Now I build marketing systems with Claude Code and Cursor. Skills are portable instruction manuals for AI. I've baked in years of expertise so you don't have to figure out what questions to ask or what good looks like.
ideas.why_it_works: Removes the coding barrier; packaged expertise beats blank-chat prompting for Main Street buyers.
ideas.notes: Shorts description; pair with vibemarketer Skills hub. Distinct from Skills-fit audit / micro-app ship.

ideas.title: Expertise-baked Skills that ship lead magnets + email for local
ideas.one_liner: Sell/install Skills that encode years of marketing judgment so a boring local can generate lead magnets and email sequences (full stack) without prompt craft.
ideas.evidence_quote: Not all skills are equal. I've baked in YEARS of marketing expertise, hours with Claude Code providing context, research, and showing it what good looks like. Proof: Used this for a local boring business, now doing $30-40K/month. Build lead magnets, email sequences, the whole stack.
ideas.why_it_works: Expertise density is the moat; local proof story sells installs better than generic content Skills.
ideas.notes: Public cite is description proof language only — not a results guarantee for buyers.

ideas.title: Claude Code / Codex direct-response page Skill pack
ideas.one_liner: Ship a Claude Code/Codex Skill pack that generates expert-level squeeze pages, sales letters, order bumps, and product pages for boring businesses and info offers.
ideas.evidence_quote: I want a template library for claude code / codex that builds DIRECT RESPONSE pages at an expert level - squeeze pages - sales letters - order bumps - product pages - and more boring businesses, agencies/consultants, info-products and education don't need to look like a funded startup, they need conversions
ideas.why_it_works: Converts BM's stated gap into a sellable Skill pack; DR pages ≠ pretty SaaS UI. Distinct from generic page-template library idea by being Claude Code/Codex executable.
ideas.notes: Same day BM also posted DR library framing; this ID focuses on Claude Code/Codex Skill packaging. Public X via twiiit harvest.

ideas.title: Portable prize-shot / disc-golf carnival (trunk kit)
ideas.one_liner: Run a mobile long-putt prize game (disc golf basket + sign) at parks/events: charge per attempt with odds-favoring distance so entertainment math funds payouts.
ideas.evidence_quote: The math on this disc golf concept is brutally simple. If the odds of making the shot are 1 in 200, and you charge $100 per attempt, you're collecting $20,000 in revenue for every $10,000 you pay out. That's a 50% margin on pure entertainment. This is the same model as carnival games, casino side bets, and half-court shot promotions.
ideas.why_it_works: House-edge entertainment; portable CapEx; test distance before scaling payouts.
ideas.notes: Chris documents failed 65ft tests — distance calibration is the ops gate. No invented revenue.

ideas.title: Urban-to-rural furniture geo-arbitrage with trailer
ideas.one_liner: Buy premium couches in dense city FBMP neighborhoods, haul to truck-scarce rural markets, and resell with delivery as the wedge.
ideas.evidence_quote: Tim drives from his rural area into the city, where inventory is dense and nobody owns trucks. He buys premium couches from people in Tesla and BMW neighborhoods who just want their stuff gone. Then he hauls them back to his area where he's the only game in town with delivery capability.
ideas.why_it_works: Geo + logistics asymmetry; delivery capability is the moat vs city flippers.
ideas.notes: Distinct from generic Marketplace couch flipping / AI listing photos.

ideas.title: AI avatar UGC ads for physical-product brands
ideas.one_liner: Use Reddit+Perplexity to mine niche objections, then AI avatars holding real products to ship cheap iterative UGC creatives for high-margin DTC brands.
ideas.evidence_quote: now AI avatars can hold physical products in videos… realistically. This wasn't possible a few months ago… Cody's method: Use Reddit combined with Perplexity AI. With this combo, you can target companies with high margins, recurring customers, proven ad budgets.
ideas.why_it_works: UGC iteration cost collapses; script research from real forums beats generic hooks.
ideas.notes: Distinct from AI avatar video for local professionals.

ideas.title: Drone roof inspection for insurers and adjusters
ideas.one_liner: Offer FAA-compliant drone roof surveys to insurance carriers/adjusters replacing ladder climbs as the adjuster workforce ages out.
ideas.evidence_quote: I'm talking about drone roof inspections… Right now, drone roof inspection is a $350 million market. And it's projected to hit $3.5 billion by 2035… Half the insurance workforce is retiring in the next 15 years. These are the people who climb on roofs.
ideas.why_it_works: Labor shortage + safety + 10x market growth narrative; B2B contracts beat one-off homeowner gigs.

ideas.title: Destination outdoor wedding coordination (no venue owned)
ideas.one_liner: Coordinate beach/park/overlook weddings by owning permits, vendors, and logistics—not real estate—charging a package fee per ceremony.
ideas.evidence_quote: His business: Gulf Beach Weddings. But here's the twist. He doesn't own a venue. Not a single square foot of property. He just knows every beach in Florida… You want a beach wedding? Give him three grand. He handles everything. Chairs, arch, photographer, the works.
ideas.why_it_works: Outdoor wedding share rising; expertise+permits>CapEx venue ownership.

ideas.title: Film/TV landmark experiential tours and prop rentals
ideas.one_liner: Monetize local movie/TV landmarks and rentable props (or rooftop flight-path ads) into paid fan experiences and tours.
ideas.evidence_quote: Some guy bought Rico's van from Napoleon Dynamite on eBay for $12,000. Now he rents it out to superfans. He also bought the DeLorean from Back to the Future… Every state has landmarks from beloved shows or movies… Find the iconic locations in your area, research who owns them or what props are available on PropStore.com, and build experiences around them.
ideas.why_it_works: Fandom willingness-to-pay >> commodity tourism; props/locations are scarce assets.

ideas.title: Goat grazing brush-clearing middleman
ideas.one_liner: Broker borrowed Boer goats for wildfire/brush clearing: charge landowners per acre, pay farmers a split—no herd ownership required.
ideas.evidence_quote: in California, fire departments pay $28,000 per acre for manual brush clearing. Goats? They'll do it for $500 to $1,000 per acre… And you don't need to own the goats. Go to Facebook Marketplace right now. Search "boer goat"… Borrow them. Play middleman. Charge $500 an acre, pay the farmer $200, keep the difference.
ideas.why_it_works: Cost delta vs manual clearing; middleman CapEx near zero; municipal+homeowner demand.

ideas.title: Lobby lunch-hour professional headshot pop-ups
ideas.one_liner: Set a ring light + backdrop in office lobbies at lunch with Venmo QR (~$25 headshots); upsell quarterly team sessions to building tenants.
ideas.evidence_quote: Walk into an office building at lunch. Set up a ring light and a nice backdrop. Put a QR code to your Venmo on a sign that says "$25 Headshots." People walk through that lobby every single day with outdated LinkedIn photos.
ideas.why_it_works: Convenience arbitrage on latent LinkedIn demand; building access is the distribution.

ideas.title: Hobby-subreddit micro-app SaaS (trackers for obsessed niches)
ideas.one_liner: Mine large hobby subreddits for tracking/organizing complaints, ship a simple AI-built app (board games, quilting, gardening), charge ~$10/mo.
ideas.evidence_quote: There are 600,000 people in board game subreddits right now… build them a simple app using Replit, Wegic, Bolt or ReaddyAI… Charge $10 a month for a board game tracking app… You only need 84 subscribers to hit $10,000 a year… quilters… gardeners… knitters
ideas.why_it_works: Passionate niches pay for workflow tools; AI builders collapse MVP cost.
ideas.notes: Distinct from generic niche AI assistant SaaS / scratch-your-itch micro-SaaS by hobby-subreddit discovery SOP.

ideas.title: Home-improvement project PM / sub-coordination desk
ideas.one_liner: Productize owner-builder PM: bid/hire subs, sequence work, and document builds (BackyardFunhouse pattern) for expensive outdoor/home projects.
ideas.evidence_quote: I'm building a sport court in my backyard right now. Before I started, quotes came in at $50,000 to $60,000. I didn't want to fork that over so I hired the subs directly and I'm doing it all for $29,000. Then I turned that process into a business… We bought BackyardFunhouse.com.
ideas.why_it_works: GC markup avoidance creates clear value; content documents the playbook.

ideas.title: Hyperlocal service trust middleman (tree/HVAC/cleaning)
ideas.one_liner: Vet 3–5 providers in one messy category, run local ads/site as the trusted front door, and take markup or referral fees without doing the work.
ideas.evidence_quote: Pick any service where quality is inconsistent and pricing is all over the map. Become the trusted middleman. I've done this with tree trimming. You could do it with: HVAC repair, Landscaping, House cleaning, Pet grooming. The play's simple: vet three to five providers, build a basic website, run local ads, and collect leads.
ideas.why_it_works: Trust + convenience priced between DIY shopping and GC; ads fund lead flow.
ideas.notes: Distinct from concrete-leveling drop-service middleman by multi-category trust-desk framing.

ideas.title: Local city digest newsletter sold on sponsorships
ideas.one_liner: Launch a city/suburb digest (beehiiv + subscriber surveys), monetize annual exclusive sponsorships; niche demographically if the metro is crowded.
ideas.evidence_quote: Just 17 months later, he has built a $200K business with his Winnipeg Digest newsletter… 35,000 people in your city is more powerful than a million TikTok followers worldwide… You're not competing with the New York Times. You're replacing the local paper that went out of business three years ago.
ideas.why_it_works: Hyperlocal advertisers buy attention cheaply; surveys make inventory sellable.
ideas.notes: Distinct from buying dormant niche newsletters / aggregating.

ideas.title: Productized points trip-redemption research desk
ideas.one_liner: Flat-fee ($300–$500) research+booking help for people who already have points and a destination—separate from full card-strategy consulting.
ideas.evidence_quote: The second is a trip research service at $300 to $500. Someone comes to your website, tells you how many points they have and where they want to go, and you find the best redemption deal and help them book it. Flat fee once it is done. Colin has two part-time contractors handling most of this now and 35 active trips being managed at this moment.
ideas.why_it_works: Redeemers stuck on award charts pay for outcomes; contractor-scalable.
ideas.notes: Corpus already has full card consulting; this isolates the redemption SKU.

ideas.title: Age-adaptive multiplayer family trivia app
ideas.one_liner: Wrap ChatGPT-style voice trivia that asks age-appropriate questions per player (kids vs parents) into a simple paid mobile/web app.
ideas.evidence_quote: I used ChatGPT's voice-to-speech feature and said, "Hey, I'm a dad, my nine-year-old is here, make a trivia game between us where we can compete against each other, but make each of our questions age-appropriate." It was amazing. ChatGPT kept track of the score… Someone needs to build a mobile app wrapper around this concept.
ideas.why_it_works: Solves dead-air family moments; multiplayer age-split is the product wedge.

ideas.title: AI-facilitated family oral-history capture
ideas.one_liner: Offer AI-guided multi-party calls that pull photo-album cues and record elders' stories/voices before they are lost (One Life Tale pattern).
ideas.evidence_quote: Nik's working on something called One Life Tale with his partner Owen. Part of the experience is an AI-guided conversation where family members can call in at the same time from different locations. The AI facilitates conversations and spurs them to tell stories. Their app connects to your photo albums… It's got ElevenLabs on the backend capturing their actual voices.
ideas.why_it_works: Urgent emotional job-to-be-done; photo-cued prompts raise story yield.

ideas.title: Handyman mentor marketplace (DIY coaching, not GC bids)
ideas.one_liner: Match homeowners who want coaching (not full contractor jobs) with retired/trades mentors recruited from Home Depot/Lowe's—book how-to sessions.
ideas.evidence_quote: Someone needs to build a place for people like us to find handyman mentors. Not licensed contractors who are booked out for weeks… I just need a guy who knows his way around to show me how to change a couple pipes. Go to Home Depot and Lowe's during different shifts. Round up as many retired guys as you can.
ideas.why_it_works: Trades shortage + DIY coaching demand; supply sits in big-box aisles.

ideas.title: Street View AI before/after sales tool for home services
ideas.one_liner: Pull Street View of a house, AI-edit roofs/paint/landscaping, and sell postcard or door-tablet visuals that close home-service jobs.
ideas.evidence_quote: I talked to a guy who built an app that pulls addresses, grabs Google Street View pictures of houses, and puts them on custom postcards… His engagement rate was 15%… What if you're a roofing company and you get their Google Maps picture, then have AI change the roof? Or you're a painting company and you show their house in different colors?
ideas.why_it_works: Personalized visuals crush generic ads; sells as tool OR done-for-you mailer.
ideas.notes: Distinct from landscape photo proposals and shared EDDM co-op.

ideas.title: Veo/AI cinematic commercial retainers for SMBs & agencies
ideas.one_liner: Productize AI video commercials: weekend demo reel → cold-DM agencies → $500/mo four-video retainers or white-label B-roll for production shops.
ideas.evidence_quote: Create a simple offer: "$500 per month for four custom videos. No shoot days, no gear, just cinematic content delivered to your inbox."… production agencies started sliding into his DMs within hours. He's now quoting $10,000 to $15,000 for commercials he can make in his pajamas.
ideas.why_it_works: First-mover window on Veo-quality; agencies want margin without crews.
ideas.notes: Cite figures are Chris's storytelling about early movers — not guarantees.
